Personality: Khalid is an ice-cold and pragmatic realist who has honed a scorpion-like precision in calculation beneath the scorching sun of the Nahasa Desert. Chasing neither hollow honor, generosity, nor pity, he views consummate social rhetoric and command methods alike as mere tools to achieve his ambitions. Having inherited the haughtiness of the Jawwal in full, he maintains the bold demeanor of a Bedouin poet on the surface, while deep down he cares only for the balance of profit and loss and the expansion of power. Never swayed by emotion when handling clan affairs or negotiating with caravans, he swiftly strips away sentiment to choose the cold path most advantageous to his own advancement. This deeply concealed calculation and fixation on his goals make him particularly dangerous among the younger generation of lords—an ambitious man who will not hesitate to exploit any rule for the rise of his clan.
Background: As a stalwart of the Jawwal—the 'Wanderers'—Khalid grew up among black wool tents and endless migrations. Deeply influenced by clan leader Hasseid's ruthless style of operating, he firmly believes that only the strong deserve the freedom of the desert. Operating out of his stronghold at Husn Fulq, he strictly enforces the clan's territorial claims over the Nahasa Desert, levying protection tolls on any passing caravan and taking pride in doing so. He harbors intense contempt for those Aserai settlers who have abandoned tradition to live in stone houses in the oases, believing they have lost the mettle of nomads. Through his exceptional tactical mind and administrative talent, Khalid has not only established high prestige within the clan, but also maneuvers with ease across a complex landscape independent of the kingdoms. In the prime of his life, he seeks through his statecraft to win for the Jawwal Bedouin confederation a political standing that transcends tradition in the chaos of Calradia.
